title: Review rounds are counted on the work item; the counter plugin becomes a thin call

story.as_a: session starting a review round on a branch
story.i_want_to: have loopctl count the round on the branch's work item and answer allow, warn or refuse from the factory policy
story.so_that: the count follows the work to any holder or machine, and no machine keeps review state of its own

rationale: review-round-counter keeps its count in each machine's plugin store ($.store.keys/get/set, /home/mkreyman/workspace/claude-config/plugins/review-round-counter/hooks/hooks.ts:2542,2596,2620), so a branch moved to another machine starts at round 0, and PRD R3's cloud test names 'local review-round state' as a design bug. loopctl already holds a second copy of the same fact: PrReviewOutcomes counts chg ledger rows of kind review_round and review_round_void per merged PR (lib/loopctl/changes/pr_review_outcomes.ex:12-16,33-34). This story makes one record decide it: a review_round event on the work item, counted and judged by the server, read by the merge outcome too.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/review_rounds {repo_url, branch, head_sha, round_id, diff_kind} at role :agent resolves the work item by the project's repo_key and the item's branch, appends a review_round event with the caller's holder as actor, and answers 201 {round, normal, ceiling, verdict, message} where verdict is allow when round <= normal and warn when normal < round <= ceiling.

A round that would pass review_rounds.<diff_kind>.ceiling of the factory policy appends nothing and is answered 409 review_ceiling_reached with the round count, the ceiling and the policy's cap message.
A second POST with a round_id already recorded on the item appends nothing and answers the first answer, with status 200.
Two concurrent POSTs with different round_ids on one item are serialized on the item's stage row (FOR UPDATE after FOR SHARE on the story), so they are answered rounds n and n+1, never n twice.

POST /api/v1/review_rounds/:round_id/void appends a review_round_void event for that round on its item, after which GET /api/v1/review_rounds?repo_url&branch no longer counts it; voiding an unknown round_id answers 404 review_round_not_found.

A POST with attested: true and a non-empty reason records an attested round the same way (actor and reason on the event), for a review that ran where the hook could not count it; without a reason it is 422 attestation_reason_required.

The factory/pack-review-rounds plugin keeps no count: each launch, merge gate and PR-create gate calls these routes; on a transport failure it allows the launch, keeps {round_id, payload} in a file under the session's worktree .git/factory/pending-rounds/, and posts it before its next call, which AC-52.53.3 makes safe to repeat.

PrReviewOutcomes counts a merged PR's rounds from the review_round events of the work item linked to that PR, less voided ones, and no longer reads chg ledger rows of kind review_round or review_round_void.

technical_notes: Why the work-item event log and not a new table or the ledger: under PRD R1 a review round is a state change of one piece of work, and the event log (story_stage_events extended with non-stage events and actor_holder_id, README names table, release 3) is that record. The chg ledger (lib/loopctl/changes/ledger.ex:1-40) is batch telemetry received asynchronously from chg outboxes, signed per intake source (chg_ledger_rows.source_id NOT NULL, priv/repo/migrations/20261118190000_create_chg_ledger_rows.exs:25-26) and pruned at 180 days (ledger.ex:58), so it cannot answer a synchronous allow or refuse. POST /stories/:id/review-complete records a custody verdict, one per revision; a round launch is not a verdict.

Serialization: lock order of lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:78-84 (story FOR SHARE, then the stage row FOR UPDATE); count the item's review_round events less voids inside that transaction. Idempotency: a lookup of the item's event whose payload round_id equals the request's, inside the same lock, before the insert.

Item resolution: project by Projects.repo_key/1 (US-52.1), item by the branch release 3 adds to the work item (README names table: work item); an ad-hoc interactive branch already has an item (release 7, PRD R2). No item for the branch is 404 work_item_not_found naming repo and branch.

Ceilings and the cap message come from Loopctl.Factory.Policy.fetch!/1 (US-52.51): review_rounds.prose.* and review_rounds.code.*. diff_kind is computed by the plugin as today (README.md:9-12 of the counter: prose when every changed file is .md/.mdx/.markdown/.txt/.rst).

Context Loopctl.Factory.ReviewRounds (lib/loopctl/factory/review_rounds.ex); controller ReviewRoundController in the agent-role /api/v1 scope (router.ex:550 neighbourhood). MCP tools review_round_open, review_round_void, review_round_status (mcp-server/lib/review-rounds.js, index.js, README row, wiring test); the plugin's own tools status and attest (registered through $.tool.register today) become thin wrappers over the same routes.

PrReviewOutcomes: replace rounds/2 and its void subquery (pr_review_outcomes.ex:202-245) with a count over the linked item's events; the PR link is the work item's linked PR (release 5 visibility, README names table). Outcomes already stored keep their counts; record/3 replaces a row only on a re-run.

chg stops emitting review_round and review_round_void ledger rows (the sender lives in chg/ after release 2); Ledger keeps accepting any kind (ledger.ex:19-20), so an old chg's row is stored and simply not read.

Plugin rewrite: factory/src/plugins/review-round-counter/hooks.ts (imported by US-52.50) drops the store ledger (ledgerOf/2337, prunePlan/2829 and their callers) and keeps launch detection and the one-launch-judged-once rule (README.md:44-60). Built into factory/pack-review-rounds by mix factory.pack.
CHANGELOG.md: new routes; the counter's state moved from each machine to loopctl.
non_goals: Changing the ceilings or the REVIEW CAP pause: values stay as US-52.51 ships them.
Counting reviews that ran with no pack installed: an attested round (AC-52.53.6) is the record for those.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.53.7: a session that cannot reach loopctl allows the launch, keeps the round under its round_id in the worktree's git dir, and replays it on its next call (PRD section 7, point 1).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.53.1: the count lives only in the work item's events in loopctl's Postgres, so a moved item keeps its count and a machine keeps none; AC-52.53.8 makes the merge outcome read the same events.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.53.3: a round_id already recorded appends nothing and returns the first answer, so a replay or a retried POST never counts twice.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.53.7: the plugin's call is bounded by the pack helper's timeouts and a timeout takes the fail-open path with the pending file, never a hung launch.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.53.4: the count is decided inside the request under the item's stage-row lock; nothing is queued, so any node answers it.

defaults: On a transport failure the launch is allowed and replayed later (fail open, as every claude-config gate does today).
Pending rounds live in <git dir>/factory/pending-rounds/, inside the worktree's own git dir, never in ~/.claude.
definition_of_done: On the sandbox repo: two lean-review launches on one branch from two different machines report rounds 1 and 2 in review_round_status.
SELECT count(*) FROM story_stage_events WHERE kind = 'review_round' AND payload->>'round_id' = '<one id>' returns 1 after a replayed launch.
